sanskrit: vaktavyam iha pṛṣṭena viniścitya viparyayam sa copadeśaḥ kartavyo yena dharmam avāpnuyāt
english: When questioned, one should answer only after first weighing the matter and its contrary; and such instruction alone is to be given as leads to the attainment of dharma.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātam upadeśe kṛte sati mahān kleśo hi bhavati tasmān nopadiśet kva cit
english: All this I have now declared to you: when instruction is given amiss, great affliction follows; therefore let no one give such instruction anywhere.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kīdṛśe puruṣe tāta strīṣu vā bharatarṣabha śrīḥ padmā vasate nityaṃ tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: In what kind of man, dear sire, or in what kind of women, O bull of the Bharatas, does Śrī, the lotus-goddess, ever abide? Tell me that, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣyāmi yathādṛṣṭaṃ yathāśrutam rukmiṇī devakīputrasaṃnidhau paryapṛcchata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this I shall relate to you, as I have seen and as I have heard, how Rukmiṇī once questioned Śrī in the presence of the son of Devakī.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇasyāṅkagatāṃ jvalantīṃ; dṛṣṭvā śriyaṃ padmasamānavaktrām kautūhalād vismitacārunetrā; papraccha mātā makaradhvajasya
english: Beholding radiant Śrī, lotus-faced, seated in the lap of Nārāyaṇa, the mother of Makaradhvaja, her lovely eyes wide with wonder, questioned her out of curiosity.

sanskrit: kānīha bhūtāny upasevase tvaṃ; saṃtiṣṭhatī kāni na sevase tvam tāni trilokeśvarabhūtakānte; tattvena me brūhi maharṣikanye
english: Which beings here do you attend upon, and beside which do you abide; and which do you not serve? O beloved of the Lord of the three worlds' creatures, O daughter of the great sage, tell me this truly.

sanskrit: evaṃ tadā śrīr abhibhāṣyamāṇā; devyā samakṣaṃ garuḍadhvajasya uvāca vākyaṃ madhurābhidhānaṃ; manoharaṃ candramukhī prasannā
english: Thus addressed by the goddess in the presence of him whose banner bears Garuḍa, Śrī, moon-faced and serene, spoke these words, sweet in utterance and ravishing to the mind.

sanskrit: vasāmi satye subhage pragalbhe; dakṣe nare karmaṇi vartamāne nākarmaśīle puruṣe vasāmi; na nāstike sāṃkarike kṛtaghne na bhinnavṛtte na nṛśaṃsavṛtte; na cāpi caure na guruṣv asūye
english: I dwell, O fair one, in the man who is truthful, bold, and capable, ever active in his work; I dwell not in the indolent man, nor in the unbeliever, the corrupter of castes, the ingrate, nor in him of broken conduct or cruel conduct, nor in the thief, nor in him who is envious of his teachers.

sanskrit: ye cālpatejobalasattvasārā; hṛṣyanti kupyanti ca yatra tatra na devi tiṣṭhāmi tathāvidheṣu; nareṣu saṃsuptamanoratheṣu
english: And those poor in energy, strength, and inner worth, who rejoice and rage at the merest trifle—in such men, O goddess, whose aspirations lie asleep, I do not abide.

sanskrit: yaś cātmani prārthayate na kiṃ cid; yaś ca svabhāvopahatāntarātmā teṣv alpasaṃtoṣarateṣu nityaṃ; nareṣu nāhaṃ nivasāmi devi
english: He who craves nothing for himself, and he whose inner self is corrupted by his own nature—in such men, O goddess, ever content with little, I never make my dwelling.

sanskrit: vasāmi dharmaśīleṣu dharmajñeṣu mahātmasu vṛddhaseviṣu dānteṣu sattvajñeṣu mahātmasu
english: I dwell in the righteous of conduct, in the knowers of dharma, in the great-souled, in those who serve their elders, in the self-controlled, in the noble who understand goodness.

sanskrit: strīṣu kṣāntāsu dāntāsu devadvijaparāsu ca vasāmi satyaśīlāsu svabhāvaniratāsu ca
english: Among women I dwell in the patient and the self-controlled, devoted to gods and brāhmaṇas, truthful in conduct, and steadfast in their own nature.

sanskrit: prakīrṇabhāṇḍām anavekṣyakāriṇīṃ; sadā ca bhartuḥ pratikūlavādinīm parasya veśmābhiratām alajjām; evaṃvidhāṃ strīṃ parivarjayāmi
english: The woman who scatters her household vessels, who acts without reflection, who ever speaks against her husband, who delights in another's house and is without shame—such a woman I forsake.

sanskrit: lolām acokṣām avalehinīṃ ca; vyapetadhairyāṃ kalahapriyāṃ ca nidrābhibhūtāṃ satataṃ śayānām; evaṃvidhāṃ strīṃ parivarjayāmi
english: The fickle, the unclean, the greedy gobbler, her devoid of steadiness, fond of quarrels, overcome by sleep and forever lying abed—such a woman I forsake.

sanskrit: satyāsu nityaṃ priyadarśanāsu; saubhāgyayuktāsu guṇānvitāsu vasāmi nārīṣu pativratāsu; kalyāṇaśīlāsu vibhūṣitāsu
english: I dwell in women ever truthful, fair to look upon, blessed with good fortune and rich in virtues, faithful to their husbands, of auspicious character and well adorned.

sanskrit: yāneṣu kanyāsu vibhūṣaṇeṣu; yajñeṣu megheṣu ca vṛṣṭimatsu vasāmi phullāsu ca padminīṣu; nakṣatravīthīṣu ca śāradīṣu
english: In chariots, in maidens, in ornaments, in sacrifices, in rain-bearing clouds, in blossoming lotus-pools, and in the autumn pathways of the stars, I make my dwelling.

sanskrit: śaileṣu goṣṭheṣu tathā vaneṣu; saraḥsu phullotpalapaṅkajeṣu nadīṣu haṃsasvananāditāsu; krauñcāvaghuṣṭasvaraśobhitāsu
english: In mountains, in cattle-pens, and in forests, in lakes bright with open water-lilies and lotuses, in rivers loud with the calls of swans and adorned by the cries of cranes.

sanskrit: vistīrṇakūlahradaśobhitāsu; tapasvisiddhadvijasevitāsu vasāmi nityaṃ subahūdakāsu; siṃhair gajaiś cākulitodakāsu matte gaje govṛṣabhe narendre; siṃhāsane satpuruṣe ca nityam
english: In rivers graced with broad-banked pools, frequented by ascetics, perfected ones, and brāhmaṇas, abundant in waters churned by lions and elephants, I ever dwell; and ever in the rutting elephant, in the bull, in the king, in the lion-throne, and in the good man.

sanskrit: yasmin gṛhe hūyate havyavāho; gobrāhmaṇaś cārcyate devatāś ca kāle ca puṣpair balayaḥ kriyante; tasmin gṛhe nityam upaimi vāsam
english: In that house where the fire-bearer of oblations is fed, where cattle, brāhmaṇas, and the gods are honored, and offerings of flowers are made in due season—in that house I ever take up my dwelling.

sanskrit: svādhyāyanityeṣu dvijeṣu nityaṃ; kṣatre ca dharmābhirate sadaiva vaiśye ca kṛṣyābhirate vasāmi; śūdre ca śuśrūṣaṇanityayukte
english: In the twice-born ever devoted to their sacred study, in the kṣatriya forever delighting in dharma, in the vaiśya intent on husbandry, and in the śūdra faithfully given to service, I dwell.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇe tv ekamanā vasāmi; sarveṇa bhāvena śarīrabhūtā tasmin hi dharmaḥ sumahān niviṣṭo; brahmaṇyatā cātra tathā priyatvam
english: But in Nārāyaṇa I dwell single-minded, with my whole being, made as it were his very body; for in him is set the mighty dharma, and there too are devotion to the brāhmaṇas and all that is dear.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ śarīreṇa vasāmi devi; naivaṃ mayā śakyam ihābhidhātum yasmiṃs tu bhāvena vasāmi puṃsi; sa vardhate dharmayaśorthakāmaiḥ
english: It is not with my body that I dwell, O goddess—that I cannot here declare; but the man in whom I dwell in spirit prospers in dharma, in fame, in wealth, and in desire fulfilled.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca strīpuṃsayoḥ saṃprayoge sparśaḥ kasyādhiko bhavet etan me saṃśayaṃ rājan yathāvad vaktum arhasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: In the union of woman and man, whose pleasure of touch is the greater? This doubt of mine, O king, you ought to resolve aright.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam bhaṅgāśvanena śakrasya yathā vairam abhūt purā
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recite an ancient tale—how of old enmity arose between Bhaṅgāśvana and Śakra.

sanskrit: purā bhaṅgāśvano nāma rājarṣir atidhārmikaḥ aputraḥ sa naravyāghra putrārthaṃ yajñam āharat
english: Long ago there was a royal sage named Bhaṅgāśvana, exceedingly righteous. Being without a son, O tiger among men, he undertook a sacrifice to obtain offspring.

sanskrit: agniṣṭuṃ nāma rājarṣir indradviṣṭaṃ mahābalaḥ prāyaścitteṣu martyānāṃ putrakāmasya ceṣyate
english: That mighty royal sage performed the rite called Agniṣṭu, hateful to Indra, which is enjoined among the expiations of mortals for one who desires a son.

sanskrit: indro jñātvā tu taṃ yajñaṃ mahābhāgaḥ sureśvaraḥ antaraṃ tasya rājarṣer anvicchan niyatātmanaḥ
english: But Indra, the glorious lord of the gods, learning of that sacrifice, sought for an opening against that royal sage of disciplined soul.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya mṛgayām aṭato nṛpa idam antaram ity eva śakro nṛpam amohayat
english: And after some time, as the king roved out on the hunt, Śakra, judging "this is the opening," cast a bewilderment upon him.

sanskrit: ekāśvena ca rājarṣir bhrānta indreṇa mohitaḥ na diśo 'vindata nṛpaḥ kṣutpipāsārditas tadā
english: Wandering on a single horse, deluded by Indra, the royal sage could no longer make out the quarters of the sky, and was tormented by hunger and thirst.

sanskrit: itaś cetaś ca vai dhāvañ śramatṛṣṇārdito nṛpaḥ saro 'paśyat suruciraṃ pūrṇaṃ paramavāriṇā so 'vagāhya saras tāta pāyayām āsa vājinam
english: Galloping this way and that, afflicted by weariness and thirst, the king beheld a most lovely lake brimming with excellent water; and plunging into the lake, dear son, he let his horse drink.

sanskrit: atha pītodakaṃ so 'śvaṃ vṛkṣe baddhvā nṛpottamaḥ avagāhya tataḥ snāto rājā strītvam avāpa ha
english: Then, when the horse had drunk, that best of kings tied it to a tree, and entering the water to bathe, the king attained womanhood.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ strīkṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā vrīḍito nṛpasattamaḥ cintānugatasarvātmā vyākulendriyacetanaḥ
english: Seeing himself turned into a woman, that best of kings was abashed, his whole being given over to anxious thought, his senses and mind confounded.

sanskrit: ārohiṣye kathaṃ tv aśvaṃ kathaṃ yāsyāmi vai puram agniṣṭuṃ nāma iṣṭaṃ me putrāṇāṃ śatam aurasam
english: "How shall I mount the horse, how shall I return to the city? I performed the rite called Agniṣṭu, and a hundred sons of my own loins were granted me—

sanskrit: jātaṃ mahābalānāṃ vai tān pravakṣyāmi kiṃ tv aham dāreṣu cāsmadīyeṣu paurajānapadeṣu ca
english: sons born of great strength. What shall I now say of them to my wives, and to the people of city and countryside?"

sanskrit: mṛdutvaṃ ca tanutvaṃ ca viklavatvaṃ tathaiva ca strīguṇā ṛṣibhiḥ proktā dharmatattvārthadarśibhiḥ vyāyāmaḥ karkaśatvaṃ ca vīryaṃ ca puruṣe guṇāḥ
english: Softness, slenderness, and timidity—these the sages, who behold the truth and meaning of dharma, have declared the qualities of woman; while exertion, hardness, and valor are the qualities of man.

sanskrit: pauruṣaṃ vipranaṣṭaṃ me strītvaṃ kenāpi me 'bhavat strībhāvāt katham aśvaṃ tu punar āroḍhum utsahe
english: "My manhood is utterly lost, and womanhood has come upon me by some agency; in this state of womanhood, how can I bring myself to mount the horse again?"

sanskrit: mahatā tv atha khedena āruhyāśvaṃ narādhipaḥ punar āyāt puraṃ tāta strībhūto nṛpasattama
english: Then with great distress that lord of men mounted the horse and, turned into a woman, returned to the city, dear son—that best of kings.

sanskrit: putrā dārāś ca bhṛtyāś ca paurajānapadāś ca te kiṃ nv idaṃ tv iti vijñāya vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ
english: His sons and wives and servants, and the folk of city and countryside, perceiving "what then is this?", were struck with the utmost amazement.

sanskrit: athovāca sa rājarṣiḥ strībhūto vadatāṃ varaḥ mṛgayām asmi niryāto balaiḥ parivṛto dṛḍham udbhrāntaḥ prāviśaṃ ghorām aṭavīṃ daivamohitaḥ
english: Then that royal sage, now a woman, best of speakers, said: "I had set out to hunt, firmly surrounded by my forces; but, deluded by fate, I strayed and entered a fearsome wilderness.

sanskrit: aṭavyāṃ ca sughorāyāṃ tṛṣṇārto naṣṭacetanaḥ saraḥ suruciraprakhyam apaśyaṃ pakṣibhir vṛtam
english: And in that most terrible wilderness, parched with thirst and bereft of my wits, I beheld a lake of most lovely aspect, thronged with birds.

sanskrit: tatrāvagāḍhaḥ strībhūto vyaktaṃ daivān na saṃśayaḥ atṛpta iva putrāṇāṃ dārāṇāṃ ca dhanasya ca
english: Having plunged therein, I was made a woman—plainly by fate, there is no doubt—as though I had not yet had my fill of sons, of wives, and of wealth."

sanskrit: uvāca putrāṃś ca tataḥ strībhūtaḥ pārthivottamaḥ saṃprītyā bhujyatāṃ rājyaṃ vanaṃ yāsyāmi putrakāḥ abhiṣicya sa putrāṇāṃ śataṃ rājā vanaṃ gataḥ
english: Then that best of kings, now a woman, said to his sons: "In harmony enjoy this kingdom; I shall go to the forest, my dear ones." And having consecrated his hundred sons, the king departed to the forest.

sanskrit: tām āśrame striyaṃ tāta tāpaso 'bhyavapadyata tāpasenāsya putrāṇām āśrame 'py abhavac chatam
english: In the hermitage, dear son, an ascetic took that woman to wife; and by that ascetic a hundred sons were born to her in the hermitage as well.

sanskrit: atha sā tān sutān gṛhya pūrvaputrān abhāṣata puruṣatve sutā yūyaṃ strītve ceme śataṃ sutāḥ
english: Then taking these sons, she said to her former sons: "You are my sons begotten in manhood, and these hundred are my sons in womanhood.

sanskrit: ekatra bhujyatāṃ rājyaṃ bhrātṛbhāvena putrakāḥ sahitā bhrātaras te 'tha rājyaṃ bubhujire tadā
english: Enjoy the kingdom together, as brothers, my dear ones." And those brothers, united, then enjoyed the kingdom together.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā bhrātṛbhāvena bhuñjānān rājyam uttamam cintayām āsa devendro manyunābhipariplutaḥ upakāro 'sya rājarṣeḥ kṛto nāpakṛtaṃ mayā
english: Seeing them enjoy that excellent kingdom in brotherly accord, Indra, lord of the gods, overwhelmed with wrath, reflected: "I have done that royal sage a service, not an injury."

sanskrit: tato brāhmaṇarūpeṇa devarājaḥ śatakratuḥ bhedayām āsa tān gatvā nagaraṃ vai nṛpātmajān
english: Then in the guise of a brāhmaṇa, the king of the gods, lord of a hundred sacrifices, went to the city and sowed dissension among those sons of the king.

sanskrit: bhrātṝṇāṃ nāsti saubhrātraṃ ye 'py ekasya pituḥ sutāḥ rājyahetor vivaditāḥ kaśyapasya surāsurāḥ
english: "There is no brotherhood among brothers, even among the sons of one father: for the sake of the kingdom the gods and demons, sons of Kaśyapa, fell to strife.

sanskrit: yūyaṃ bhaṅgāśvanāpatyās tāpasasyetare sutāḥ kaśyapasya surāś caiva asurāś ca sutās tathā yuṣmākaṃ paitṛkaṃ rājyaṃ bhujyate tāpasātmajaiḥ
english: You are the offspring of Bhaṅgāśvana, while the others are the sons of an ascetic—just as the gods and the demons were the sons of Kaśyapa; yet your paternal kingdom is being enjoyed by the ascetic's sons."

sanskrit: indreṇa bheditās te tu yuddhe 'nyonyam apātayan tac chrutvā tāpasī cāpi saṃtaptā praruroda ha
english: Set at variance by Indra, they struck one another down in battle; and hearing this, the ascetic-woman, sore stricken, broke into weeping.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇacchadmanābhyetya tām indro 'thānvapṛcchata kena duḥkhena saṃtaptā rodiṣi tvaṃ varānane
english: Approaching her in the disguise of a brāhmaṇa, Indra then inquired: "With what grief are you tormented, that you weep, O fair-faced one?"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaṃ tu tato dṛṣṭvā sā strī karuṇam abravīt putrāṇāṃ dve śate brahman kālena vinipātite
english: Seeing the brāhmaṇa, that woman piteously replied: "My two hundred sons, O brāhmaṇa, have been laid low by time.

sanskrit: ahaṃ rājābhavaṃ vipra tatra putraśataṃ mayā samutpannaṃ surūpāṇāṃ vikrāntānāṃ dvijottama
english: I was once a king, O brāhmaṇa, and there a hundred sons were begotten by me, handsome and valiant, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: kadā cin mṛgayāṃ yāta udbhrānto gahane vane avagāḍhaś ca sarasi strībhūto brāhmaṇottama putrān rājye pratiṣṭhāpya vanam asmi tato gataḥ
english: Once, gone out to the hunt, I strayed in a dense forest and, plunging into a lake, was made a woman, O best of brāhmaṇas; and having established my sons in the kingdom, I then withdrew to the forest.

sanskrit: striyāś ca me putraśataṃ tāpasena mahātmanā āśrame janitaṃ brahman nītās te nagaraṃ mayā
english: And to me as a woman a hundred sons were begotten by a great-souled ascetic in the hermitage, O brāhmaṇa; these too I brought to the city.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ ca vairam utpannaṃ kālayogena vai dvija etac chocāmi viprendra daivenābhipariplutā
english: And by the working of time enmity arose among them, O brāhmaṇa; this I lament, O best of brāhmaṇas, overwhelmed by fate."

sanskrit: indras tāṃ duḥkhitāṃ dṛṣṭvā abravīt paruṣaṃ vacaḥ purā suduḥsahaṃ bhadre mama duḥkhaṃ tvayā kṛtam
english: Seeing her in her grief, Indra spoke harsh words: "Of old, O lady, you wrought me grief most hard to bear,

sanskrit: indradviṣṭena yajatā mām anādṛtya durmate indro 'ham asmi durbuddhe vairaṃ te yātitaṃ mayā
english: by performing a sacrifice hateful to Indra, slighting me, O perverse one. I am Indra, O foolish one, and the enmity I have requited upon you."

sanskrit: indraṃ tu dṛṣṭvā rājarṣiḥ pādayoḥ śirasā gataḥ prasīda tridaśaśreṣṭha putrakāmena sa kratuḥ iṣṭas tridaśaśārdūla tatra me kṣantum arhasi
english: But seeing Indra, the royal sage fell with bowed head at his feet: "Be gracious, O best of the gods; that sacrifice was performed by me in longing for sons, O tiger among the gods; in this you ought to forgive me."

sanskrit: praṇipātena tasyendraḥ parituṣṭo varaṃ dadau putrā vai katame rājañ jīvantu tava śaṃsa me strībhūtasya hi ye jātāḥ puruṣasyātha ye 'bhavan
english: Well pleased by her obeisance, Indra granted a boon: "Which of your sons, O king, shall live? Tell me—those born to you as a woman, or those who came to you as a man?"

sanskrit: tāpasī tu tataḥ śakram uvāca prayatāñjaliḥ strībhūtasya hi ye jātās te me jīvantu vāsava
english: Then the ascetic-woman, with reverently folded hands, said to Śakra: "Let those who were born to me as a woman live, O Vāsava."

sanskrit: indras tu vismito hṛṣṭaḥ striyaṃ papraccha tāṃ punaḥ puruṣotpāditā ye te kathaṃ dveṣyāḥ sutās tava
english: But Indra, astonished and delighted, questioned that woman again: "How are the sons you begot as a man become hateful to you?

sanskrit: strībhūtasya hi ye jātāḥ snehas tebhyo 'dhikaḥ katham kāraṇaṃ śrotum icchāmi tan me vaktum ihārhasi
english: How is it that your love is greater for those born when you were a woman? I wish to hear the reason; this you ought to tell me here."

sanskrit: stry uvāca striyās tv abhyadhikaḥ sneho na tathā puruṣasya vai tasmāt te śakra jīvantu ye jātāḥ strīkṛtasya vai
english: The woman said: A woman's love is the greater—not so a man's; therefore, O Śakra, let those live who were born to me when I was made a woman.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam ukte tatas tv indraḥ prīto vākyam uvāca ha sarva eveha jīvantu putrās te satyavādini
english: Bhīṣma said: When she had spoken thus, Indra, well pleased, replied: "Let all your sons live here, O truthful one.

sanskrit: varaṃ ca vṛṇu rājendra yaṃ tvam icchasi suvrata puruṣatvam atha strītvaṃ matto yad abhikāṅkṣasi
english: And choose a boon, O lord of kings, whatever you desire, O steadfast in vows—manhood or womanhood, whichever you crave from me."

sanskrit: stry uvāca strītvam eva vṛṇe śakra prasanne tvayi vāsava
english: The woman said: I choose womanhood itself, O Śakra, since you are gracious, O Vāsava.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu devendras tāṃ striyaṃ pratyuvāca ha puruṣatvaṃ kathaṃ tyaktvā strītvaṃ rocayase vibho
english: Thus addressed, Indra, lord of the gods, replied to that woman: "How is it that, forsaking manhood, you prefer womanhood, O mighty one?"

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca strībhūto rājasattamaḥ striyāḥ puruṣasaṃyoge prītir abhyadhikā sadā etasmāt kāraṇāc chakra strītvam eva vṛṇomy aham
english: Thus addressed, that best of kings, now a woman, replied: "In the union of woman and man, the pleasure of the woman is ever the greater; for this reason, O Śakra, I choose womanhood itself."

sanskrit: rame caivādhikaṃ strītve satyaṃ vai devasattama strībhāvena hi tuṣṭo 'smi gamyatāṃ tridaśādhipa
english: "And I take greater delight in womanhood—truly, O best of gods; I am content in my woman's state. Go now, O lord of the gods."

sanskrit: evam astv iti coktvā tām āpṛcchya tridivaṃ gataḥ evaṃ striyā mahārāja adhikā prītir ucyate
english: Saying "So be it," and taking leave of her, Indra departed to heaven. Thus, O great king, is the woman's pleasure declared the greater.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃ kartavyaṃ manuṣyeṇa lokayātrāhitārthinā kathaṃ vai lokayātrāṃ tu kiṃśīlaś ca samācaret
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What ought a man to do who seeks the welfare that sustains worldly life? And of what conduct should he be as he carries on the course of the world?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kāyena trividhaṃ karma vācā cāpi caturvidham manasā trividhaṃ caiva daśa karmapathāṃs tyajet
english: Bhīṣma said: Of action by the body there are three kinds, by speech four kinds, and by the mind three; these ten paths of evil action one should renounce.

sanskrit: prāṇātipātaṃ stainyaṃ ca paradāram athāpi ca trīṇi pāpāni kāyena sarvataḥ parivarjayet
english: The slaying of living beings, theft, and intercourse with another's wife—these three sins of the body one should utterly shun.

sanskrit: asatpralāpaṃ pāruṣyaṃ paiśunyam anṛtaṃ tathā catvāri vācā rājendra na jalpen nānucintayet
english: Idle babble, harshness, slander, and falsehood likewise—these four sins of speech, O lord of kings, one should neither utter nor even ponder.

sanskrit: anabhidhyā parasveṣu sarvasattveṣu sauhṛdam karmaṇāṃ phalam astīti trividhaṃ manasā caret
english: Freedom from coveting another's goods, good will toward all beings, and the conviction that actions bear fruit—this threefold course one should practice with the mind.

sanskrit: tasmād vākkāyamanasā nācared aśubhaṃ naraḥ śubhāśubhāny ācaran hi tasya tasyāśnute phalam
english: Therefore let a man do no evil by speech, body, or mind; for doing deeds good or evil, he tastes the fruit of each in turn.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitāmaheśāya vibho nāmāny ācakṣva śaṃbhave babhrave viśvamāyāya mahābhāgyaṃ ca tattvataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O mighty one, declare to me the names of the grandsire-lord, of Śambhu, of Babhru, of him who is the māyā of the universe, and his exalted majesty in truth.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca surāsuraguro deva viṣṇo tvaṃ vaktum arhasi śivāya viśvarūpāya yan māṃ pṛcchad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: O preceptor of gods and demons, O divine Viṣṇu, it is you who ought to speak that which Yudhiṣṭhira asks of me concerning Śiva, who has the universe for his form.

sanskrit: nāmnāṃ sahasraṃ devasya taṇḍinā brahmayoninā niveditaṃ brahmaloke brahmaṇo yat purābhavat
english: The thousand names of the god, which were proclaimed of old by Taṇḍin, sprung from Brahmā, and were once set forth before Brahmā in the world of Brahmā.
